provenance.orgName: Campsey, Suffolk. Priory of St Mary the Virgin, of Augustinian nuns
provenance.p: The 1744 sale catalogue of the Harley library describes an inscription that was subsequently washed off: 'On the last Leaf, there is a Memorandum, written by a Nun of Campesey, named Elyzabeth Wyllowby, That she gives this Book to Dame Cateryne Symonde, under the Condition, That, in no wise, she sell it, or give it from the House of Campessey: But she shall give it to one of her Sisters.' (Catalogus Bibliothecae Harleianae, III, no. 1560.)

Under ultra-violet light, 'Elizabeth Willowby' and 'dame Cateryne Symonde' are more or less legible (sig. H6v). The writing matches that in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS 268, also once owned by Elizabeth Willowby.

history.provenance: Elizabeth Wyllowby, nun of Campsey Priory (Suffolk) to Catherine Symond.
Thomas Rawlinson (1681--1725), his sale, part VIII, 26 April 1727, lot 2072
Acquired by Edward Harley (1689--1741), 2nd earl of Oxford. With other printed books from his library, sold by his widow, Henrietta Cavendish (1694--1755), in 1743 to Thomas Osborne.
George Spencer Churchill (1766-1840), 5th duke of Marlborough and Marquess of Blandford
White Knights Library sale, Evans, part I, 7 June 1819, lot 970 for £32/11/0 to:
Heneage Finch (1786--1859), 5th earl of Aylesford, for whom the book was rebound (his crest is on the binding), which is probably when the inscription was removed.
Heneage Finch (1849-1885), 7th earl of Aylesford, his sale, Christie's, 12 March 1888, lot 409, to Quaritch.
William Amhurst Tyssen-Amherst, Baron Amherst (1835--1909), his sale, Sotheby's London, 3 Dec. 1908, lot 180 (purchased prior to sale) to: Pierpont Morgan (1837--1913).
Purchased for Princeton with the Amherst collection, 1908.
